# Registering on PROSPERO

A dose-response protocol has to commit to choices that a standard protocol never
mentions. This chapter walks the registration field by field.

Every `##` section gets its own figure, as in Chapter 1. One H2 is one slide, so
the figure is also that slide's visual, and a section without one leaves the
deck with a blank.

## Why register a dose-response review

What pre-registration protects against when the analysis has many defensible
shapes.

## The fields that differ from a standard review

Exposure definition, dose scale, and the planned functional form.

## Committing to a model before seeing the data

Declaring two-stage or one-stage, the spline basis, and the knot placement in
advance, and how to phrase a contingency without writing a blank cheque.

## Declaring the dose metric

The unit, the reference level, and how open-ended categories will be assigned.

## Planned sensitivity analyses

Which modelling choices will be varied, and which results would change the
conclusion.

## A worked record

The registration for the physical activity review [@garcia2023] read as a model
to copy.
